reason: E2 supports the general premise that twinning can enhance both strength and ductility. E1 shows twinning occurs in an FCC HEA under high strain rates, but neither passage provides evidence that adding ductile-phase-forming elements to a BCC RHEA will induce a metastable FCC phase or activate twinning in that system. The critical link between the intervention and the mechanism in refractory alloys is unsupported.
premises: Mechanical twinning can simultaneously improve strength and ductility in metallic materials.
Twinning is promoted in materials with low stacking fault energy (SFE).
Adding elements that form a metastable FCC phase can lower SFE and activate twinning.
Twinning is an active deformation mechanism in some HEAs under high strain rates.
The proposed intervention will induce a metastable FCC phase in a primarily BCC RHEA.
